questions.text: V1. Which word means "a plan made of ordered steps"?
questions.explanation: Algorithm: A plan made of ordered steps.

questions.text: V2. Which word means "instructions written so a computer can run them"?
questions.explanation: Program: Instructions written so a computer can run them.

questions.text: V3. Which word means "the order in which instructions run"?
questions.explanation: Sequence: The order in which instructions run.

questions.text: V4. Which word means "an object on screen with appearance, size, and location"?
questions.explanation: Sprite: An object on screen with appearance, size, and location.

questions.text: V5. Which word means "an action a sprite keeps doing until stopped"?
questions.explanation: Behavior: An action a sprite keeps doing until stopped.

questions.text: V6. Which word means "a trigger that causes instructions to run"?
questions.explanation: Event: A trigger that causes instructions to run.

questions.text: V7. Which word means "code that repeats instructions"?
questions.explanation: Loop: Code that repeats instructions.

questions.text: V8. Which word means "finding and fixing errors in code"?
questions.explanation: Debugging: Finding and fixing errors in code.

questions.text: 4.1. The Artist faces right, moves 50 pixels, turns right 90 degrees, then moves 30 pixels. Which path results?
questions.explanation: A right turn from facing right points down.

questions.text: 4.2. Which code draws a square with 40 pixel sides?
questions.explanation: Four equal sides and 90 degree turns make a square.

questions.text: 4.3. Which turn should replace 60 degrees when drawing an equilateral triangle?
questions.explanation: The outside turn is 360 divided by 3, or 120 degrees.

questions.text: 5.1. A fish is small, blue, and near the top. Which describes its location?
questions.explanation: Location describes where a sprite is.

questions.text: 5.2. A fish swims right and spins. Only spinning is stopped. What continues?
questions.explanation: Stopping one behavior does not stop the other.

questions.text: 5.3. Your tank should have a swimming fish and wandering turtle. Which is the best test?
answers: Run and check both sprites against the plan
questions.explanation: Test each sprite and its intended behavior.

questions.text: 6.1. How are an algorithm and a program related?
answers: An algorithm is a plan; a program is runnable instructions
An algorithm is a sprite; a program is its costume
An algorithm is an error; a program fixes all errors
An algorithm must use blocks; a program cannot
questions.explanation: A program expresses a plan as computer instructions.

questions.text: 6.2. Which order makes sense when building a spinning cat scene?
answers: Add spinning to cat; create cat; run and check
Run and check; add spinning; create cat
Create cat; add spinning; run and check
Create cat; check finished result; add spinning
questions.explanation: Create the sprite before starting its behavior, then test.

questions.text: 6.3. You want a small cat to spin, but a large dog spins. What should you inspect?
answers: The targeted sprite, its costume, and its size
questions.explanation: Check the target sprite and its properties against the plan.

questions.text: 7.1. Which example shows a career using computer science?
answers: A musician edits recordings with software
questions.explanation: Audio software uses computing to create and edit music.

questions.text: 7.2. Which career scene includes a user event and a response?
answers: Click a chef sprite and it explains recipe software
A chef stays still with no event code
A kitchen background has no sprites
The title contains the word chef
questions.explanation: The click triggers the explanation.

questions.text: 7.3. What should you do when remixing a classmate’s project?
answers: Change the title and claim all the work
Ask permission only if someone notices
Get permission, credit the creator, and keep Remix in the title
questions.explanation: The slides direct students to get permission and give credit.

questions.text: 8.1. In “When Right is pressed, move the dog right,” what is the event trigger?
questions.explanation: The key press triggers the movement response.

questions.text: 8.2. A bird wanders and spins. Space stops wandering only. What will it still do?
questions.explanation: Spinning has not been stopped.

questions.text: 8.3. A sprite should jump on Up, but nothing happens. Which check is most useful?
answers: Check the key event and its action for the intended sprite
Rename the project and assume it is fixed
Change the background and stop testing
Add a costume without checking the event
questions.explanation: Check the trigger, connected response, and target sprite.

questions.text: 9.1. Which plan gives a pet two different user interactions?
answers: Create the pet; set its starting size
Choose a background; choose a title
Click it to say Hello; press Space to spin
Create the pet; set its starting location
questions.explanation: Clicking and pressing Space are distinct user events.

questions.text: 9.2. A spinning pet should rest without spinning when clicked. Which response works?
answers: Change costume but leave spinning active
Stop spinning, then show a resting costume
Start spinning again and show a resting costume
Make it larger but leave spinning active
questions.explanation: Changing a costume alone does not stop spinning.

questions.text: 9.3. A partner cannot tell how to use your pet. What is the best improvement and test?
answers: Add hidden controls and do not test
Change the title and assume it is clear
Remove all events and ask if it looks nice
Add controls instructions and ask the partner to try them
questions.explanation: Clear instructions help the user trigger intended actions.

questions.text: 10.1. A dance changes after four measures of four beats each. How many beats have passed?
questions.explanation: 4 measures times 4 beats equals 16 beats.

questions.text: 10.2. A new move is under a Left arrow event. You click Run but press no arrow. What happens to that event?
answers: It runs after any key is pressed
It waits for Left to be pressed
It runs when the dancer grows
questions.explanation: Clicking Run does not itself trigger the Left arrow event.

questions.text: 10.3. Which pairs an appearance change with a movement event?
answers: Make the dancer larger; change its color
Make the dancer larger; change its move on Right
Change moves on Right; change moves on Left
Rename the project; choose a song
questions.explanation: Size affects appearance; a key event can change movement.

questions.text: 11.1. Button 1 triggers drums. Button 2 triggers a bell. You press only Button 2. What is triggered?
questions.explanation: Only the matching Button 2 event is triggered.

questions.text: 11.2. Why use an event for a surprise sound that a player should control?
answers: It lets the player choose when to trigger the sound
It forces the sound to play only at the start
It makes every sound play together
It removes the need for input
questions.explanation: An event can wait for the player’s input.

questions.text: 11.3. An echo is assigned to Button 1 for a mysterious scene. Which test checks the event and mood?
answers: Run without pressing a button and assume it works
Press Button 2 and check the title
Run, press Button 1, and judge if the echo suits the scene
Check only the number of blocks
questions.explanation: Trigger the assigned event and listen in context.

questions.text: 12.1. Which loop repeats the whole chunk move forward; move forward; turn right three times?
answers: Repeat 3 [move forward; move forward; turn right]
Repeat 2 [move forward; move forward; turn right]
questions.explanation: All three commands belong inside the loop, repeated three times.

questions.text: 12.2. Trace repeat 4 [move forward; move forward]; then turn left once. What happens?
questions.explanation: Two forward moves repeat four times; the turn is outside.

questions.text: 12.3. BB-8 needs six forward moves. Code says repeat 5 [move forward]. Which fix works?
answers: Add a turn inside the loop
questions.explanation: One forward move repeated six times gives six moves.

questions.text: 13.1. Starting at position 0 facing right, trace repeat 4 [stamp; move forward 30]. Where are the stamps?
questions.explanation: Stamping happens before each move, starting at 0.

questions.text: 13.2. Starting at position 0 facing right, which code stamps stars at 0, 25, 50, 75, and 100 pixels?
questions.explanation: Stamp first, then move, for five repetitions.

questions.text: 13.3. All your repeated stamps land on one spot. Which instruction is probably missing?
answers: Return to the starting spot before every stamp
Move to a new position between stamps
questions.explanation: Movement or repositioning separates the stamps.
